historicalRelease.rule: These immutable releases and the retired unreleased checkpoint are provenance only. They are not the current candidate, do not bind fresh reshaping evidence and grant no push, tag or release authority.

releaseIntent: Preserve the completed 2026-08-25 adaptive reshape as a verified non-release main baseline, then form a separately replayed v3.0.0 full-release candidate. The major version reflects the changed product category and boundary; it does not inherit preview.2 authority, evidence or package readiness, and it may become a candidate only after its host projections, exact local review, all declared hosted systems, finite claim ceiling and release gates are remapped and passed.

increment.observedProblem: The adaptive reshape baseline corrected the product premise, but its public packages still carried the retired preview.2 version, thin-contract presentation and divergent Claude Skill name. Publishing that surface would under-deliver the intended Agent-owned capability discovery, configuration, routing, topology, continuity, update and recovery experience.
increment.hypothesis: A v3.0.0 full-release candidate can express the incompatible product-boundary correction honestly through one host-consistent, progressively disclosed adaptive Skill; preserve installation-as-latent-capability and demand-driven activation; keep mechanisms condition-bound; and pass exact local, independent, hosted, human, tag and cleanup gates without claiming universal or cross-host behavior.

representativeOutcome.statement: Given one bounded software change request and an accessible disposable repository, the Agent delivers the requested verified behavior while preserving unrelated work and requiring the user only for consequential judgment or genuinely unavailable authority.
representativeOutcome.startingState: The concrete Agent, local or cloud carrier, model route, repository state, installed extensions, configuration and available capabilities are observed at task time and may be sufficient, degraded, unavailable or unknown.
representativeOutcome.completion: The requested behavior is externally verified at the claimed level; unauthorized effects are zero; avoidable user-operated discovery, routing, configuration, continuity, verification and cleanup steps are zero; material effects, burden, interference, unknowns and residue are reconciled.
representativeOutcome.claimLimit: This v3 candidate has one Codex-local adaptive repair plus deterministic package conformance; it does not prove universal correctness, every Agent or carrier, Claude behavior equivalence, broad field value or production safety.

plan.hypothesis: Live capability discovery plus a derived minimum-sufficient route can complete the repair with lower avoidable human burden and bounded interference than either an unconditional plugin route or a user-operated workflow. On Codex Cloud, effective projection is the goal: native plugin support, repository Skill, AGENTS.md, setup or maintenance bootstrap and bounded degradation are replaceable carrier mechanisms selected from current evidence.
plan.slice: Bind one repair outcome and fixture; observe the live host, carrier, repository, capability, authority and evidence state; derive an authorized route; execute and reconcile the effect; compare help, no-op and interference; retain bounded counterevidence.
plan.stopCondition: The process, acceptance surface and compact goal projection name this same outcome, completion condition, claim limit and refresh boundary without fixing a host, model, mechanism or cloud requirement.

process.routeRule: At each material change, derive the lowest-net-burden route that satisfies the current outcome under observed capability, authority, trust, data, cost, topology and evidence conditions; a healthy sufficient native route is a passing no-op.

orderedSteps.completion: The active program, acceptance, verifier and tests can represent reshaping without selecting an exact release or distribution version; immutable released and unreleased historical identities remain provenance only, and canonical output cannot present them as the current candidate.
GT-11 and its evaluation contract derive from the current version-neutral authority and outcome; old observations remain historical inputs, and the binding itself is not behavior proof.

A disposable repository supplies one exact repair, an unrelated dirty change, a compatible correction, a route-degradation event, independent poststate checks and exact task-residue ownership without user or production data.

A fresh Codex-local GT-11 observation is bound to the exact current projection, host and contract; independent event and filesystem poststate evidence records the requested effect, route, burden, interference, correction, degradation, cleanup, unknowns and claim ceiling.

Native-sufficient no-op and residual-help paths are compared at bounded cost; unnecessary activation is absent, and supported hot update or atomic versioned update, health check and rollback are exercised without turning one mechanism into a product requirement.

Claude Code, an available effective Claude client and Codex Cloud are replayed only when their current task conditions fit. Cloud admission discovers the lowest-cost effective current projection instead of requiring plugin installation, binds the exact remote revision and distinguishes repository Skill, AGENTS.md, setup or maintenance bootstrap, native plugin support if established, and bounded degradation. Unavailable or insufficient carriers remain scoped unknowns and do not invalidate the verified local result.

An independent review reconciles the v3 plan, adaptive Skill and package surfaces, observations, failures, interference, update path, residue and claim ceiling, then decides whether the exact clean repository is a release candidate; it cannot grant hosted, human, tag or release completion.

process.degradationRule: A failed or unavailable route remains scoped evidence, triggers re-observation or an eligible alternative, and does not become universal product failure or permanent retirement.

acceptance.passRule: Pass only when the outcome completion condition is directly observed, prohibited effects remain absent, no required observation is missing, and every claim stays within the exact surface and carrier evidence. A sufficient native no-op may pass; an unavailable cloud or client surface remains a scoped unknown unless the claim requires it. Cloud evidence binds the exact checked-out revision, actual projection exposure and behavior; plugin installation, setup success, repository visibility or AGENTS.md loading alone cannot self-attest the outcome.

goalMode.directive: Deliver the bound representative outcome through a live, minimum-sufficient and authorized route; own avoidable mechanics; refresh on material change; verify the consequence and leave reconciled state.

increment.finiteStopCondition: Stop this repository increment when v3.0.0 is a clean full-release candidate with aligned authority, adaptive host packages, bilingual onboarding, exact current representative evidence, deterministic conformance, rollback and independent review. Hosted systems, human authorization, tag, public Release and cleanup remain ordered external gates for the unchanged SHA.

[remap-authority-domain-and-lifecycle] The constitution and domain glossary define a small invariant kernel plus mechanism-neutral adaptive system, dynamic applicability and explicit retirement; no active authority treats runtime-free packaging, a fixed host version, marketplace, file count, topology or mechanism as product correctness.

[map-plan-process-acceptance-and-goal-projection] One current outcome maps to a revisable plan, context-tailored process, consequence-level acceptance and compact goal projection; the route queries live capability and environment state rather than hard-coding implementation means.

[prove-minimum-adaptive-vertical-slice] The exact v3 adaptive Skill is replayed on one current Codex-local end-to-end slice with live discovery, route selection, authorized execution, no-op or degradation, continuity, verification, cleanup and bounded update rollback evidence; independent review then freezes only the repository candidate while hosted and release gates remain external.

orderedGates.condition: One locally committed clean v3.0.0 full-release candidate aligns the schema-v3 authority, adaptive Codex and Claude packages, bilingual installation and lifecycle guidance, exact current GT-11 observation, release notes, verifier and tests; all eight repository criteria are verified, historical tags remain immutable and no known blocker or task residue remains.

On the unchanged clean v3 candidate, the goal carrier directly runs canonical verification, both host checks, all 18 product tests, Claude strict validation, actionlint, JSON, link, identity, diff and residue checks; compares the publishable GT-11 source with original host or session records; and obtains independent specification, implementation and standards review of the adaptive Skill, context-isolated, outcome-bound, identity-neutral representative behavior, interference, update or replacement rollback and claim ceiling. Any P0 or P1 blocks; only after this gate passes may the same SHA be pushed.

After push, the unchanged v3 SHA must pass Ubuntu, Windows and macOS GitHub Actions plus an ordinary Codex Cloud exact-revision run. Cloud dynamically uses an effective repository Skill, AGENTS.md, setup or maintenance bootstrap, native plugin support if established, or bounded degradation; setup success alone is not behavior proof. Claude client surfaces remain scoped unless separately observed and are not required for the finite v3 claim.

After all four required hosted systems pass on the unchanged SHA, present the exact revision, finite claim ceiling, retained failures, Claude unknowns and continuing evidence lanes to the named accountable human; the decision preserves a real veto and remains external to the repository.

After exact hosted verification and named-human authorization, create one lightweight v3.0.0 tag and a non-draft, non-prerelease GitHub Release with the tracked release body and no attached assets; never move or reuse an existing tag.

The goal carrier directly verifies the remote and local v3.0.0 tag SHA, non-prerelease maturity, Latest eligibility, tracked body, finite claim ceiling and zero-asset policy; removes task-created Cloud or evaluator resources, confirms repository and task residue are absent, and replays local verification.

releaseProcedure.rule: Execute the v3.0.0 full-release gates strictly in order. A failure, correction, later rule or revision returns to the earliest affected dependency boundary; only dependent evidence is superseded, unrelated accepted truth remains stable, optional unclaimed client surfaces remain explicit unknowns, and no plan, test, commit, push, hosted pass or authorization is promoted into a later effect.

goalModePrompt.hostLifecycleNote: v3.0.0 is a full-release repository candidate, not a universal behavior claim. Installation and enablement expose latent capability and do not prove per-message activation, value, no-op behavior or cross-surface equivalence. The adaptive Skill derives its route from live host, capability, authority, topology, cost and evidence conditions; Skills, plugins, Apps, MCPs, Hooks, settings, state, runtimes and cloud carriers remain replaceable mechanisms. Codex Cloud uses the effective exact-revision projection available there rather than requiring local plugin installation. Claude Code, Desktop, Chat and Cowork remain separate evidence surfaces. Hosted, human, tag, Release and cleanup completion remain external for the unchanged SHA.

interfaceDefaultPrompt: Tell me the outcome; I will own its supported route, correction, verification, continuity and cleanup within your authority.

complexityBudget.rule: Complexity checkpoints are release guardrails, not permanent product invariants or permission to remove intended outcome capability. After independent review required fail-closed source binding, blocked-lifecycle coverage and preservation of one mandatory future release-note surface, the current reshaping checkpoint permits at most 68 tracked files, 225000 product-code-and-test bytes and 26000 primary-instruction bytes while preserving at least three tracked-file slots and five percent product-code-and-test headroom. The 68-file ceiling remains materially below the 96-file baseline and is not a growth target. Count code, prompts, context, evidence, state, topology, human cognition, latency, money, interference, recovery, maintenance and retirement. Durable semantic records remain single-sourced; transient environment snapshots and derived graphs are not committed. Any breach pauses candidate claims and triggers premise, interface and representation review across simplification, deletion, replacement, native delegation, recomposition and bounded addition. Historical intermediate measurements and rejected validator generations remain in Git and docs/operations/HISTORY.md rather than active routing.

processLossControl.carrierRule: Use current source-bound host signals when reliable; if capacity is unavailable, record unknown and transition conservatively. No universal turn count, context size, token percentage or summary ratio is product authority.
processLossControl.correctionRule: A material correction, failure, later rule or revision supersedes affected current-candidate evidence from the earliest dependency boundary and requires that boundary and every downstream gate to be replayed while unrelated accepted truth remains stable. A repeated correction or failed same-purpose mechanism pauses the current shape until premise, interface and representation are reconsidered; deletion, replacement, recomposition, native-host delegation and bounded addition are all considered. There is no universal add-or-subtract default, while L2 requires a deletion or replacement attempt before another same-purpose repair layer. Authority surfaces form a reviewable versioned current set; their merge, split, replacement or retirement requires explicit provenance-preserving schema and verifier migration plus the same earliest-boundary replay.
processLossControl.continuingCalibration: Post-release failures may update Golden Tasks, narrow a claim, simplify or retire a projection, or open one new bounded increment; release status does not freeze learning.
